summary: Two failed kernel-run attempts while trying to run a kaggle_benchmarks task via CLI push.
what_happened: v1 push: papermill ValueError 'No kernel name found in notebook' - generated ipynb lacked top-level nbformat/nbformat_minor keys and cell id.
v2 push (nbformat fixed): kernel executed but failed with ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'kaggle_benchmarks'.
root_cause: kaggle_benchmarks is not installed in the standard image used by CLI-pushed kernels. Its LLM resolution requires MODEL_PROXY_URL + MODEL_PROXY_API_KEY (kaggle_benchmarks/kaggle/models.py), which only the Benchmarks-task runtime injects; the model gpt-6-astra exists only on that platform proxy (not on the user's local gateway, not pip-installable-with-creds). Benchmark tasks therefore must be created via the Kaggle Benchmarks UI, which provisions the runtime kernel (pattern: new-benchmark-task-* kernels).
fixes_applied: nbformat 4/5 + cell id added (needed for any CLI-pushed notebook)
kernel metadata id must equal title-derived slug or SaveKernel returns 409
lesson: To run a kbench task: author the task .py (base64 content + @kbench.task + LLM_DEFAULT=gpt-6-astra setdefault pattern), then create the task through kaggle.com/benchmarks UI; afterwards fetch results with kaggle kernels output on the generated kernel slug.
